done_when: forge story new <KEY> "<title>" works for a story that has no spec: the story's own branch adds it to the roadmap, the plan's Why carries the problem, and the story gets one read loop and one approval; stories made from a spec work as today and specs stay optional. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body: Raise: Functional. This new check reads the fix worktree, so an agent can add the required roadmap entry and run promotion before committing it. Promotion then renames the fix branch, but `_promote` commits only the state files; the SPEC task branch has no committed roadmap entry to deliver. This is distinct from the earlier promotion finding: the new refusal covers missing and default-only entries, but accepts an entry present only as a local edit. The promotion test covers committed, missing and default-only entries, not this state.
findings.title: Promotion accepts an uncommitted roadmap entry and leaves it off the task branch

stop.reason: Owner chose narrow: a fix promoted to a story keeps today's roadmap route; only brand-new stories start from a one-line goal

why: A new story needs a spec, its own read loop, a confirmation and a roadmap fix before its plan can even start
